final.executive_summary: Hold AAPL and let the existing 4.882 shares (~1.5% of $99,596, ~$1,493 at the 305.93 mark) ride: execution_action = keep_shares, target_weight_now = null, no trade at the next open. The five consecutive trims from 15% to 1.5% already did the de-risking, so a further cut pays 10bps to remove a ~$125 tail while forfeiting the only equity optionality in a 98.5%-cash book, and an add at 305.93 buys into a ladder of sellers (VWMA 314.11, 50SMA 309.19, 10EMA 309.46, Bollinger mid 318.43) with sub-1:1 reward to the first target against a 1.5xATR stop. Both the bull and the bear independently named the same confirmation — a close above 309.5 on >50M shares — so the correct pre-trigger action is to do nothing and keep the ladder narrative, not implemented: ~2.0-2.5% on that close, the full 4-5% only on a subsequent close above 318.4 that also reclaims the 314.11 VWMA, with any added length re-anchored to a fresh 1.5xATR stop rather than the parked 294 level. Horizon 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October 10-Q.
final.investment_thesis:
The neutral analyst wins this debate, and it wins because it is the only seat that sized the decision correctly rather than arguing about a decimal. The position is $1,493 of a $99,596 book that is 98.5% cash; the marginal trade in either direction costs more in fees than the tail risk it moves. That is the decisive arithmetic, and both extremes fail it.

The aggressive analyst reaches the right conclusion on the wrong spine. His "$58 maximum loss" is not a maximum: it is computed from a 294 level the plan itself labels a narrative condition, and AAPL has already demonstrated it can vault such a level — 333.43 to a 304.81 open on 7/31, a 28.6-point overnight hole on 132.5M shares. His fee comparison fails outright on the authoritative account ($44.42 cumulative fees is not fifteen times $58, and sunk cost is irrelevant to the next dollar). His claim that 304.81-333.43 is "air" ignores the single most defended supply shelf on the chart: the 20-day VWMA at 314.11 leaves that cohort underwater, the August high of 316.29 is a lower high against July's 344.57, and the bounce sequence 75.05M -> 68.00M -> 49.44M -> 46.14M -> 34.44M -> 28.23M is decaying volume into resistance, the signature of a failing rally, not accumulation. Most importantly he never prices his own ladder: adding 4-5% at 318.43 with a stop at 294 nearly doubles the distance to the protective level (3.9% from 305.93 versus 7.7% from 318.43), turning a $58 stub risk into roughly $380.

The conservative analyst's process is better but his conclusion overcalls. His "realistic worst case is the whole $1,493" is a solvency case, not a stress case; the neutral's correction is right — the honest stress is a repeat of the 7/31 gap plus follow-through to the rising 200SMA at 280.48, which costs about $125 on 4.882 shares. His appeal to the five prior trims is the same fallacy he correctly attacked in the aggressive's fee argument: those trims already achieved their purpose, moving 15% -> 6.5% -> 4% -> 2.5% -> 1.5%, and cutting 1.5% to zero de-risks nothing while paying 10bps to remove the book's only equity optionality. Where he is right and I adopt it: 294 is inside the noise given ATR 7.86 and a demonstrated gap risk, so if the position ever becomes material the real invalidation is the 300-302 shelf on expanding volume and the structural line is 280.5. He is also right that the falling Bollinger mid — 324.37 on 7/31 to 318.43 on 8/14, roughly 0.6 points a session — marks the first target down while the risk stays put, which argues for a high bar on adding, not for selling.

Where the evidence genuinely sits — balanced, not forced. The bear leg is factual: eleven consecutive closes below a rolling 50SMA at 309.19, price 2.61% under the 314.11 VWMA, MACD below zero and below signal, a 10/50 cross within twenty-seven cents with the 10EMA falling ~1 point a session, RSI 43.67 that never reached 30 even on the -7.35% gap day (patient sellers, not flushed sellers), and an entirely unfilled 304.81-333.43 gap. The bull leg is equally factual and is why this is not Underweight: the primary trend is intact (price ~9.1% above a rising 200SMA at 280.48), the MACD histogram has contracted three sessions (-3.634 to -2.648) while price made a marginally lower low, three rising intraday lows (300.57 -> 302.05 -> 304.30) sit directly on the 300 floor, ATR has compressed ten sessions from 9.872 to 7.861, Q3 FY26 delivered 50.06% gross margin (+357bp) on $109.42B revenue (+16.4%) with operating income +26.6% and EPS +28.7%, net cash of $62.2B roughly doubled in nine months with zero new long-term debt, and buybacks re-accelerated to $25.1B. The bull's §2 math is the decisive fundamental exchange: +225bp gross margin and -42bp SG&A fully funded a +115bp R&D ramp and still left net operating margin +152bp — operating leverage, not a deteriorating business, and the bear never refuted it.

Crucially, both sides named the same trigger independently: a close above 309.5 on >50M shares (the bear's falsification condition is the bull's confirmation condition). When that happens, the pre-trigger stance is do nothing, not pre-position. The conservative's four-condition simultaneous gate (309.5 + >50M + positive histogram + higher low) is too strict — it only opens after the gap has substantially filled, converting the add into chasing — while the aggressive's "top of the range" sizing ignores the risk-unit drift. The neutral's ladder splits the difference correctly: first tranche 2.0-2.5% (~$2,500) on a volume-confirmed reclaim of the 309.2-309.5 cluster, second tranche to 4-5% only on a close above 318.4 that also reclaims the 314.11 VWMA, and a mandatory re-anchor of the stop to the prevailing 1.5xATR from any new entry.

Prior record binds this call. AAPL Underweights on 07-20 through 07-24 and 07-31 each bled 3.2% to 13.6% of five-day alpha by cutting inside a stacked rising trend on momentum decay; the 08-07 Hold cost -2.7% alpha, whose lesson was to commit the invalidation level in advance and size from arithmetic rather than conviction. The one pre-event Underweight that worked (07-28, -13.1% alpha) worked because a dated binary catalyst then hit — and that 7/31 event has already printed and been absorbed once. That asymmetry is why the residual core stays.

What would change the call. Upgrade: a daily close above 309.5 on >50M shares -> rebalance toward 2.0-2.5%; a subsequent close above 318.4 with expanding volume and acceptance above the 314.11 VWMA -> the full 4-5%. Downgrade: repeated rejection at 314.11 with a fresh MACD rollover below signal, or a close below 300.00 on expanding volume (breaks the 300.57/302.05/304.30 floor; next shelf 292.27) -> cut to zero; a close below 280.48 (200SMA) exits regardless of any fundamental view; gross margin below 48-49% converts the inventory build from a monitoring item into a genuine de-rating cause and overrides the technical triggers toward zero.

Explicitly missing and not assumed: no iPhone/Mac/Services or geographic segment breakout, so a 50% gross margin as mix shift versus a favorable cost/pricing window cannot be verified; no guidance; no analyst revisions for 7/31; no options chain or implied volatility; no flows/positioning data; no valuation multiples; no explanation of the 7/31 gap catalyst; no reconciliation of the $13.27B intangible step-up against $13.53B of new noncurrent liabilities (an unexplained monitoring item, not a thesis breaker — the conservative is right that it is a disclosure gap, the aggressive wrong to treat it as optionality); and the China LLM item is single-source with a "coming months" timeline that produced 67 cents on the lightest volume in four months — optionality, not a position driver. Those gaps cap conviction and are why this is a token Hold rather than a rebuild.
